name: Empedocles
credit: Engraving from Thomas Stanley's History of Philosophy, 1655 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Empedocles of Acragas (Agrigentum) in Sicily was a Greek philosopher, physician and poet of the fifth century BC. He wrote in hexameter verse and taught that all things are made from four roots, fire, air, earth and water, which Love draws together and Strife pulls apart in endless cycles.

This archive carries the 1 epigram ascribed to the poet in the third volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation of the Greek Anthology (Book IX: 569), and William Ellery Leonard's verse translation of the surviving fragments of his poems On Nature and The Purifications.

poems.title: Book IX, 569: From his book “On Nature”
poems.author: Empedocles
poems.note: Paton marks the second part with the remark “(From his Purifications)”.
poems.text: I have been a boy and a girl, a shrub, a bird, and a warm-blooded fish of the sea. Hail! my friends who dwell in the citadel of the great city, yellow Agrigentum, observers of righteousness. Know that I, no longer a mortal, but an immortal god, sojourn here honoured by all as is meet, crowned with fillets and flowery garlands.
